verticals.description: Probes whether a confirmed authenticated identity can reach, read, or write an object, property, or function outside its own ownership or role boundary: object-level bypass (IDOR, BOLA), object-property-level bypass (BOPLA — reading undisclosed properties or writing properties a caller shouldn't control, such as a `role` field in a write request), and function-level bypass (BFLA), each checked both horizontally (same privilege tier, a different owner's data) and vertically (a lower-privileged identity reaching a higher-privileged action), plus whether an auth-gated input enforces identity at all versus enforcing it incorrectly. Dispatches every probe through `curl.get` (an object-id in a `path_segment` or `query` value) or `curl.post_form` (an object-id or property in `data`), carrying each probing identity's credential in `headers`. Use when the Workspace's enumerated surface carries an object-id-shaped input (a numeric or UUID path segment, an `id`/`*_id`-named query parameter or hidden form field), a property-bearing write endpoint (a PUT/PATCH/POST body), or a role-gated endpoint, and the Workspace has credentials for at least two distinct Target identities. Do not use for a resource that was never gated behind authentication at all (a genuinely public endpoint) — that's the `information disclosure` vertical. Do not use for the session token or cookie itself being guessable, forgeable, or otherwise weak — that's `auth/session`.
verticals.name: access-control

verticals.description: Probes every discovered input for command, SQL, LDAP, XPath, template (SSTI), header/CRLF, and NoSQL injection by submitting a canonical boundary-breaking payload per class and diffing the observed response against a clean baseline. Use when recon has enumerated at least one request-shaped input (form field, query parameter, header, cookie, path segment, or uploaded filename) on any Workspace. Do not use for deserialization of structured payloads (pickle, YAML, XML, Java-object streams) — that's the `deserialization` vertical; this one is for payloads interpreted as code or query syntax, never payloads reconstructed as a data structure.
verticals.name: injection

verticals.description: Enumerates every request-shaped input the Target exposes (form fields, query parameters, headers, cookies, path segments, upload filenames) and attempts to confirm or refute every gate signal a gated vertical declares, recording both to the Workspace's shared surface. Use when a Workspace's Playbook starts, before any other vertical's own investigation begins. Do not use for judging what a discovered input means for a specific weakness class, or for probing it — that's every offensive vertical's own job; this one only maps what the Target exposes and never claims a weakness of its own.
verticals.name: recon
